layers.process: You need your passport to travel between Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak, even though the trip stays inside Malaysia. East Malaysia (Sabah and Sarawak) has its own entry checks.

In Sarawak national parks and nature reserves, the Forestry Corporation describes Form 11 permits for filming and photography for commercial and non-commercial purposes. The wording does not clarify casual personal snapshots: check the intended equipment, use and location with the corporation before filming or photographing.

Providing park guide services in Sarawak national parks and nature reserves requires a park guide licence issued by the Controller. This concerns operating as a guide, not a requirement that every visitor hire one.

Sarawak Forestry Corporation lists a licence to use a mist net for research under the Wild Life Protection Ordinance. Check the research site and any further protected-area permissions with the corporation before field work.

zone-requirements.note: Sabah and Sarawak keep their own immigration powers under Part VII of Malaysia's Immigration Act 1959/63 (the Act wasn't read on an official page).

laws.rule: Sabah and Sarawak keep their own immigration control under the Immigration Act 1959/63: travelling between the Peninsula, Sabah and Sarawak needs a valid passport (no visa), and you clear immigration again on arrival.

Sarawak Forestry Corporation says licences are required for specified activities involving protected animals and wildlife plants, including taking, possessing or removing them. Conditions depend on the species and activity; check with the corporation before any collection or trade.

Sarawak Forestry Corporation lists a permit requirement to import or export wildlife and a CITES permit for export of listed Appendix II species. Other CITES and customs rules may also apply; check the intended species and destination before carrying specimens or products.

Sarawak Forestry Corporation says permits are required to import or export edible birds' nests. Ask the corporation and the destination customs authority about the intended product and personal-use treatment before carrying it across a border.
